n: Payroll, Employee, Insider Fraud and Collusion
ds: Employees or contractors abuse access to divert funds, create ghost employees, falsify expenses or collude with outsiders. Weak segregation of duties and unchecked privileged access raise risk.

src.t: ACFE, Occupational Fraud 2024: A Report to the Nations (2024)
Fraud Advisory Panel (UK), guidance on internal fraud (general)
COSO and ACFE, Fraud Risk Management Guide (2016)

rat: Ghost employees, expense and vendor fraud within payroll and procurement flows, committed by staff; also bank staff abusing privileged access.

ind.n: Ghost employee or duplicate bank account on payroll
ind.cx: Payroll records show employees without HR evidence or shared bank details.
ind.ds: Payroll records show employees without HR evidence or shared bank details.

ind.n: Expense claims just below approval limits
ind.cx: Pattern of claims under thresholds or with duplicate receipts.
ind.ds: Payments, claims or contracts are broken into amounts just under internal authorisation limits.
ind.cn: Payments or claims split to stay below internal approval limits

ind.n: Employee never takes leave or resists rotation
Excessive access or override of controls
ind.cx: Privileged users bypass approvals or alter records.
ind.ds: Employees override approvals, alter records, access records without need or show unusual relationships with customers.
ind.cn: Staff override of controls or excessive record access

ind.cx: Staff accounts credited from customers, vendors or dormant accounts.
ind.ds: Staff accounts credited from customers, vendors or dormant accounts.

ind.n: Vendor with staff-linked address or bank details
ind.cx: Procurement or payment to entity linked to an employee.
ind.ds: Vendor has no verifiable address, tax number or deliveries, or shares address or bank details with an employee.
ind.cn: Vendor linked to employee or without verifiable existence

ind.cx: Repeated complaints or unauthorised changes by one employee.
ind.ds: Repeated complaints or unauthorised changes by one employee.

ind.n: Alterations to payroll or master data outside cycle
ind.cx: Changes made around pay run by one user.
ind.ds: Changes made around pay run by one user.

ctl.ds: Matches accounts, devices, identifiers and beneficiaries against industry fraud sharing and ingests law-enforcement, commercial and open-source threat feeds, including victim reports from other institutions. It catches known bad actors early.

ctl.n: Sampling, quality assurance and analytics audit
ctl.ds: Takes periodic samples of customer files, alert decisions, relied-upon files or analytical datasets and tests them for exceptions, duplicates and errors, feeding findings back to owners and training. It independently confirms that controls work as designed.

ctl.n: Segregation of duties and dual authorisation
ctl.ds: Ensures no single person can create, approve and release a payment or master-data change, requiring an independent second approver. It controls insider and impersonation fraud.
Rules that alert on abnormal count, value or speed of movements over defined windows compared with customer profile and peer norms. They provide baseline coverage across many typologies.

Provides protected, confidential channels for staff, workers and suppliers to report misconduct or concerns, together with conduct monitoring to surface insider collusion. It brings internal and supply-chain issues to light.
Tracks cases, outcomes, losses and false positives, routes concerns across fraud, sanctions and anti-corruption teams and feeds outcomes into tuning and appetite. It supports consistent handling.

Reviews and updates customer information on a risk-based cycle and when triggers occur, such as ownership change, key attribute change, adverse information or out-of-profile activity. Fresh data keeps risk ratings and expected-activity baselines current.
Analyses typing, navigation, remote-access tooling, call-in-progress signals and deviation from baseline to spot coached, scripted or hijacked sessions. It detects coercion and takeover.

Tests bidding and award data for rotation, cover bids, price clustering, splitting, variations and exceptions to competition, and requires independent cost and justification review. It detects collusion and corrupt awards.

ctl.n: Vendor master-data and bank-detail change control
ctl.ds: Requires independent verification and review of any new or changed supplier bank details before the next payment run, including challenge of redirections to third-country accounts. It stops payment-diversion and business-email-compromise fraud.

Trains branch, contact-centre and relationship staff to ask open questions, recognise coaching, coercion, pressure and evasion and escalate with authority to pause. It strengthens the human control at the point of contact.
